title: Capstone: show the record high after each game
idea: GUIDED CAPSTONE. Track a running best and print it each pass — the max pattern, but reporting progress as it builds.
problem: For scores [3, 7, 5, 9], print the best-so-far after each game: 3, 7, 7, 9.

exercises.prompt: PROBLEM: after each score in [3, 7, 5, 9], print the record high so far. OUTPUT is...
options: A best-so-far value after each game (several lines)
exercises.explanation: Output is a running report — one best-so-far per game, not just the final max.

exercises.prompt: How does this differ from plain 'find the max'?
options: We print the current best every pass, not just at the end
exercises.explanation: Same max tracking, but we report progress each step. The pattern is reused, the reporting changes.

exercises.prompt: Example by hand. best starts at 3 (first game). After 3, print 3. Next 7 > 3, best = 7, print...
exercises.explanation: 7 beats 3, best updates to 7, we print 7. Each line is the record AFTER that game.

exercises.prompt: Next 5 (not > 7) print 7; then 9 > 7 print 9. Full output?
exercises.explanation: 3, 7, 7, 9 — the best never drops. That's our check sequence.

exercises.prompt: Plan it. Order the per-pass steps.
blocks: If the score beats best, update best
Start best at the first score
exercises.explanation: Seed best, then each pass: update if bigger, then print the current best. Printing comes after the possible update.

exercises.prompt: Why print best AFTER checking the new score, not before?
options: So the printed record already includes the newest game
exercises.explanation: We want the record THROUGH the current game, so update first, then print. Sequencing is the puzzle here.

exercises.prompt: Code the loop body. Arrange the lines.
exercises.explanation: Check-and-maybe-update first, then print best. The print sits at the loop's indentation, outside the if.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the update test:

scores = [3, 7, 5, 9]
best = scores[0]
for score in scores:
    if score ____ best:
        best = score
    print(best)
exercises.explanation: Use > to raise the record. Prints 3, 7, 7, 9 — the best-so-far after each game.

exercises.prompt: Run it: prints 3, 7, 7, 9. Hand matched. Verdict?
exercises.explanation: Matches. A running max that reports progress — same pattern, new use.
best seeds 5; 2 doesn't beat it (print 5); 8 does (print 8). Output 5, 5, 8. The record only ever rises.
